contributions.statement: When the only input is a JavaParser fact list for one design-pattern class, do not prefer Mixtral over a conservative SWUM realiser on token overlap: cosine similarity favored Mixtral (0.3351 vs 0.2532) but BERTScore F1 did not (0.8799 vs 0.8754, median difference 0.001, not significant) on 150 paired files.
contributions.evidence: §5.1 Table 2 and the Wilcoxon tests on 150 pairs. Absolute cosine stays about 0.33. The model is instructed to use only the DPS JSON, not source (§4.2.2). The conciseness ranking is a separate unvalidated Llama judge and does not survive Bonferroni (§5.2).

reason: The significant separator is cosine similarity among three realisers of the same JSON, not a comprehension or multi-repo documentation result. The conciseness rule and the 20/40/60/80-word runs do not survive the tables, so this stays a metric caveat rather than a harness gate.
